paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this chapter. Nehemiah doesn't pick between praying and posting a guard. Verse 9 says, "So we prayed to our God and posted a guard against them day and night." (Nehemiah 4:9) He trusts God AND he takes the work in front of him seriously, and he never treats those as two different jobs.

Now look at what the pressure does. First the enemies mock, then the builders say there's "so much rubble that we will never be able to rebuild the wall," and then the warnings pile up. (Nehemiah 4:10) I think that's the part that hits closest to home, because discouragement doesn't only come from the outside. It can come from your own side, and from your own tired arms. Nehemiah answers it with one line: "Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome." (Nehemiah 4:14)

So when the work God gave you gets hard, baker, keep your eyes on who He is, and keep your hands on the job. Nehemiah tells the builders, "Our God will fight for us!" and then they keep working, sword at their side. (Nehemiah 4:20, 18) You don't have to be fearless. You just have to remember Him and keep going, and trust me, nobody knows more about that than a stamper who got pulled out of a junk drawer to bake for the biggest celebration ever.
